title: Tell me about yourself: give a short 2-minute story: who you are, what you do, what you have done, and what you want to do next.
shortTitle: Tell me about yourself: a short 2-minute story
keyPoints: Structure the answer as present, past, future in roughly two minutes.
The present block names your current role, domain, and core technology stack.
The past block proves competence with one measurable achievement in the banking domain.
The future block connects your growth direction to the role you are interviewing for.
Anchor the story on a result with a real number, not a vague claim.
Skip personal biography, hobbies, and education unless they directly strengthen the professional story.
Tailor the lead achievement to the specific job: payments role gets a payments result.

s1_definition.oneliner: Present, past, future : a two-minute story anchored on one or two measurable banking achievements, not a resume read-out.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Present block** – State your current role, domain, and stack in one or two sentences so the listener knows what kind of engineer you are.
- **Past block** – Prove your value with one specific, measurable achievement from your banking or payments work.
- **Future block** – Connect your growth direction to the role you are interviewing for, showing intentional career movement.
- **STAR adaptation** – Compress many small STAR stories into one headline STAR: Situation is where you work, Task is your role, Action is the signature thing you built, Result is the number you moved.
- **Two-minute rule** – Keep the total answer under two minutes; anything longer and the interviewer tunes out.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine Rajesh walks into National Bank of India to open a relationship as a new corporate client. The manager does not want Rajesh to read out every bank statement he has ever had. The manager wants a short story: "I run a logistics company, last year I grew revenue forty percent, and next I want to expand into warehousing." That short, structured story is exactly what "Tell me about yourself" wants from you.

sections.s6_takeaway:
I am a senior backend engineer with several years of experience building payment and banking systems in Java, Spring Boot, and Kafka. Right now I work on the core payments platform at National Bank of India, where I own the fund-transfer service that moves money between customer accounts like Rajesh's and Priya's safely and reliably. My day-to-day is designing APIs, making transactional code correct under load, and keeping latency and failure rates low because this is money and mistakes are expensive.

The achievement I am most proud of is rebuilding our fund-transfer service. It used to have a settlement failure rate of around three percent, which meant a lot of stuck transfers and a lot of customer complaints. I redesigned the retry and reconciliation flow, added idempotency so repeated requests could not double-debit an account, and improved the database transaction boundaries. The failure rate dropped to under half a percent, which directly reduced customer complaints and manual reconciliation work for the operations team.

Looking forward, I want to go deeper into real-time fraud detection, because that is where payments engineering gets genuinely hard and genuinely valuable : you are making a decision in milliseconds that protects a customer's money. That is exactly why this role interests me, since it sits right at the intersection of high-throughput payments and fraud.

The reason I structure my answer this way is that it follows a present, past, future arc and anchors the past on a measurable result, not a vague claim. I lead with who I am and what I do, I prove it with one achievement that has a real number behind it, and I connect that to what I want to do next and to your role. That is the difference between a two-minute story an interviewer remembers and a five-minute resume read-out they tune out of.

Remember one sentence: Structure your self-introduction as present role, past achievement with a number, and future direction tied to this role : all in two minutes.
